# codebone

> codebone gives AI coding agents a live architecture map of a repository through MCP.

## Canonical links
- Website: https://codeb.one/
- Repository: https://github.com/palusc/codebone
- Releases: https://github.com/palusc/codebone/releases
- Benchmark: https://github.com/palusc/codebone-benchmark
- Changelog: https://github.com/palusc/codebone/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

## Current release
- Version: 1.7
- License: MIT
- Platform: macOS 13+ on Apple Silicon (arm64)
- Built-in map model: Qwen2.5-Coder 0.5B with Apple Metal acceleration
- Storage: local SQLite
- Server: localhost-only MCP and HTTP API

## Core behavior
codebone watches a selected project and builds a live graph from deterministic source facts and grounded local synthesis. It extracts routes, tables, models, events, imports, business domains and flow summaries. Shared entities connect files even when they do not import one another.

## Agent tools
- `cb()` returns a project overview.
- `cb(query="...")` returns ranked, focused context with source evidence.
- `cb(file="...")` returns context and links for one file.
- `codebone_tldr()` returns a compact project summary.
- `codebone_status()` reports the active local instance.

## Supported clients
Any MCP-compatible client can use codebone. Project setup paths include Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini/Antigravity and opencode.

## Privacy boundary
With the built-in map agent, source analysis, inference and SQLite storage run locally. Environment files, private keys and credential-like files are excluded. Optional cloud BYOK providers are explicit; enabling one can send relevant source to that provider.

## Benchmark boundary
The project-maintained benchmark automatically runs the same four-part task in two isolated agent sessions against a generated 160+ file SaaS project. It records tokens and timing, verifies four behaviors outside the editable projects, and writes a plain-English verdict. It is a reproducible harness, not independent validation, and should not be used to claim a universal percentage improvement without recorded runs. Its codebone arm uses a static fallback graph and fixed task-derived queries, not live MCP calls or local-model synthesis. The generated repository is a compact sample, not a production-scale project.
